label: Time clock: privileged duration versus any order-preserving coordinate
resolution: Metric finiteness, spaced descents and the spaced Reaper premises are defined relative to a clock, and they are not invariant under reparametrization: a bounded clock (arctan) makes every integer past metrically finite and the spaced premises vacuous there; a logarithmic clock (ln t on the positive reals) makes every open-below finite past metrically infinite, so the spaced premises would again target FLRW-shaped histories. The Lean results of MetricGrimReaper are stated for an arbitrary clock, CLOCK_2, and hold for every one; the statements, the conclusion and the objection audit are read with the clock instantiated by the physically privileged duration, CLOCK_1 (cosmic or proper time). In particular the claims that the FLRW and Benardete objections have no target in the spaced premises hold under CLOCK_1, where an FLRW past has finite duration. No argument passes from one sense to the other: the theorems never use any property distinguishing CLOCK_1, and the choice of CLOCK_1 is an open interpretive commitment, motivated by duplication recombination (duplicates keep their intrinsic, proper duration) and contested by Misner-type logarithmic time (a lead, not read).
